Country.evidence_source: Two researchers initially recruited participants from Harare using an opportunistic method of sampling. Once data collection in Zimbabwe was complete, the same two researchers recruited an age-matched sample of Zimbabwean women in London using a snowball-sampling technique.

Survey method.evidence_source: All participants provided informed consent and completed paper-and-pencil surveys in which the order of presentation of the scales was counterbalanced.

Source of sample.evidence_source: Two researchers initially recruited participants from Harare using an opportunistic method of sampling. Potential participants were approached in public spaces and invited to take part in a study on women's health. Once data collection in Zimbabwe was complete, the same two researchers recruited an age-matched sample of Zimbabwean women in London using a snowball-sampling technique.

Number of studies.evidence_source: The text describes a single study with two distinct recruitment phases/samples (Harare and London).

section_summary.extract_value: This section describes the procedure for a single study, detailing ethical approval, the use of English for the survey, and participant recruitment. Participants were recruited from Harare, Zimbabwe, using opportunistic sampling, and an age-matched sample of Zimbabwean women in London, UK, using snowball sampling. All participants completed paper-and-pencil surveys.
